$comment: SHARED-CONSTANT REGISTRY. Created by the corpus-audit agent, wave 0, to close BAR-CRITIQUE-01 G7 and W4. RULE: a number used by more than one reference item has EXACTLY ONE owning item. Every other item that uses it CITES it and may not restate a different value. A second definition of an owned constant is a corpus defect, reported by tools/corpus-index.mjs --check under the constants rule of RI-MTH05. Where an item's number deliberately differs from the owner's, it is recorded in `deliberate_divergences` below and is NOT a defect. Append-only, like subsystems.json.

how_to_use.adding_a_constant: If your item states a number another item will need, register it here with your item as `owner` before you finish. If the number already exists with a different owner, do not restate it - cite the owner.
how_to_use.consuming_a_constant: Name the owning item inline, e.g. `walk speed 2.0 m/s (RI-WLD01, seam S17)`. Never re-derive.
how_to_use.changing_a_constant: Only the owner may change the value. When it changes, every item in `consumers` must be re-derived, not re-argued.
how_to_use.diverging_deliberately: Add an entry to `deliberate_divergences` naming the item, the value, and why. An unrecorded divergence is a defect; a recorded one is a design decision.

AMENDED wave 0 (rebase-s22): DELIBERATELY NOT REBASED under seam S22. It is a human reaction-time bar with its wall-clock value stated in the row itself, not a Souls tick count, and reaction time did not change when the animation tables were corrected. Consequence: with the base rows doubled the floor no longer binds any class - the smallest contextual product is now DGR roll.r1 at 7 f@60 - so DGR and FST keep the contextual speed advantage the clamp used to confiscate. The clamp stays as a guard.

Our fixed simulation step. EVERY frame count in this corpus is at 60 Hz.

THE UNIT FINDING. Souls community frame counts - DS1, DS3 and Elden Ring alike - are quoted in 1/30-second ticks. A Souls figure of N frames is 2N of ours. Verified arithmetically: DS3's Carthus Bloodring raises i-frames 'from 12 (.4 sec) to 16 (.533 sec)', and 12/0.4s = 30 fps exactly (PROVENANCE-UPGRADE-02-SOULS section 0).

Every frame figure in RI-CMB01, RI-CMB02, RI-CMB05, RI-CMB08, RI-AI02, RI-AI03, RI-WPN01-06 and RI-CAM04 is now doubled and states its unit as f@60. RI-CMB03 is deliberately excluded (its 42 f pause was derived from 0.70 s and was already correct). The RI-CMB07 exemplar trace is INVALIDATED and awaits regeneration. Full record: corpus/00-doctrine/REBASE-S22-REPORT.md.
